newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. T-bond volatility scrapes bottom.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. T-bond volatility scrapes bottom.

text.p: Implied volatilities for Treasury bond options continued to erode Monday, sliding to historically low levels after a post-employment report nosedive on Friday.
With less than two weeks to go before expiration, June options saw volatility slump to 7.20 percent from 7.95 percent at the opening.
"Seven-point-two, that's ridiculous," said an options analyst on the bond floor. "We had a steady erosion all day long as far as volatility levels."
June options go off the board May 16. July options move to front-month status Sunday evening.
At 7.2 percent, June implied volatility is lodged near the bottom of bond options' historic range of 7.0 percent to 11.0 percent, traders noted.
September was holding up better, at 8.10 percent late in the day, down from 8.35 percent on the opening.
Interest in buying September 120-00 calls continued from last week, with two dealers seen purchasing 2,000 contracts apiece today.
Eurodollar options volatility came under follow-through pressure from late last week, as the market put a week of important economic numbers behind it, said traders at the CME.

September volatility was 8.70 percent in the 94.00 straddle, compared with 10.00 percent in the 93.75 straddle on Friday. The December 93.75 straddle was 10.70 percent, down from 11.50 percent previously.

Floor traders said the session's highlight was a combined purchase of 3,500 one-by-two put spreads in short-dated June midcurve options. Two separate firms bought the 93.50 puts and sold double the amount of 93.25 puts.
